title: Agricultural Production, Irrigation, Climate Change, and Water Scarcity in India

summary.about: Examines how climate change and limited water supplies could reshape Indian agriculture, irrigation, land use and welfare.
summary.audience: Agricultural, water, climate and food-security policymakers.
summary.method: Combines an advanced multi-sector computable general equilibrium (CGE) model with biophysical crop-yield projections and water-scarcity constraints. Counterfactual outcomes are evaluated against a calibrated baseline through sectoral output, trade, factor-income, and welfare channels.
summary.insights: Water scarcity reverses possible climate-related gains, reduces irrigation and could create welfare losses of about $3.2 billion in 2030. These are scenario-conditioned comparative responses rather than unconditional forecasts.
